text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Albania battles to regain order: People throng harbour in attempt to flee; Italian ports strained with refugees.
- Unity elusive after BQ vote: Two rivals snub new party leader.
- Rosenberg was spy, controller reveals: Ethel didn't do 'anything for us.'
- Liberal strategists in dither over campaign 'spin.'
- Isle of death finally a memorial: Canada is restoring a tiny uninhabited Quebec site where thousands of Irish refugees died in quarantine 150 years ago.
- Quebec unshaken by exodus: Montreal builds its own francophone business class after ceding title of financial capital.
- Eaton's gives vultures another high-risk target: They're 'gambling' that the chain's debt will be worth more later than now.
- Fireworks blazes into show business: In one year, the fledgling entertainment firm has hit nearly C$100-million of film and TV production, nipping at the heels of the majors.
- TSE 300 bear count on the rise.
- Ottawa struggles with budget gap: Most departments seem to be lagging well behind on delivering Martin's promised spending cuts.
- McCain snaps up Ore-Ida for US$500 million from Heinz.
- Michael Price: Wall Street's value-hungry wunderkind.
